whyTitle: Why do forms ask for a 50KB photo?
whyP1: A 50KB cap keeps application servers fast and storage costs down when thousands of applicants upload photos at once — which is why it's such a common limit on Indian government recruitment portals. SSC CGL, UPSC, IBPS bank exams, and several state PSC and railway recruitment forms all specify a photo or signature size limit in this range, and uploads over the limit are simply rejected at submission.
whyP2: The problem is that a photo straight off a phone camera is usually 2-5MB — 40-100x too large. Resizing dimensions alone doesn't reliably hit an exact KB target, which is what this tool does directly: pick 50KB, upload your photo, and download a file sized right for the form.
howP: Your photo is re-encoded to land at or under 50KB while keeping it readable for a small ID-style image, usually with no visible quality loss. If you need a different size, the same tool supports custom targets like 20KB or 100KB too.
diveTitle: What to know about the 50KB middle ground
diveSubtitle: Why this is the default limit most portals pick.
dive1Title: Why 50KB is the most common general-purpose limit
dive1Desc: 50KB gives enough headroom for both a clear ID-style photo and a signature scan to look sharp, while still being small enough to keep upload servers fast. That balance is why it's the default many recruitment and application portals settle on.
dive2Title: How exact-target compression differs from a quality slider
dive2Desc: A generic compressor set to a fixed quality percentage gives you an unpredictable file size depending on the photo. This tool works backwards from the size — 50KB — and finds the highest quality that still lands at or under that number.
dive3Title: Both photos and signatures usually fit comfortably
dive3Desc: Unlike a tight 20KB cap, 50KB is generous enough that most passport-style photos and signature scans reach the target without visible quality loss — you're less likely to see compression artifacts at this size.
dive4Desc: The tool reduces encoding quality first, since that has the least visible impact. Only if a photo still can't fit 50KB at reasonable quality does it also shrink the pixel dimensions slightly — this rarely happens at 50KB unless the source photo is unusually large or detailed.
dive5Title: Where a 50KB limit typically shows up
dive5Desc: Recruitment application photo uploads, resume/profile picture fields, and several university admission portals commonly specify 50KB as their photo size cap — check your specific form, since some use it for signatures instead of photos.
dive6Title: What makes a photo harder to compress at the same KB target
dive6Desc: A busy, colorful background pushes file size up faster than a plain one at the same quality level — a grayscale scan or a photo with a simple background will generally look sharper at 50KB than a colorful photo with lots of fine detail.
faq1Q: Which exams and forms need a 50KB photo or signature?
faq1A: Most Indian government exam and recruitment portals — SSC, UPSC, IBPS, Railway RRB, and many state PSC forms — cap the photo or signature upload at 50KB. The exact limit varies by form, so double-check the instructions on your specific application before uploading.
faq2Q: Will compressing to 50KB make my photo blurry?
faq2A: Not noticeably for ID-photo or signature use. The tool lowers JPEG quality first and reduces pixel dimensions slightly only if it has to, so a small ID-style photo or signature stays readable.
faq3Q: What image formats can I compress to 50KB?
faq3A: JPG, PNG, and WEBP are all supported. Most exam portals ask for JPG specifically — if yours does, just upload your photo in any format and the compressed download will be sized correctly regardless.
faq4Q: Do I need to sign up or install anything?
faq4A: No. Upload your photo, get your 50KB file, done — no software to install, and the file is deleted from our servers automatically afterward.
faq5Q: Can I compress multiple photos at once?
faq5A: Yes — up to 2 images at a time on the free plan (10 on Starter, 20 on Pro). Each one is compressed to 50KB individually, and you can download them all when they're ready.
